provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the lilies work (2026-10-18): every character from the floras in the lilies notes (plantgen-claude project-files/lilies/SOURCES.md), drawn by the rules its taxa hold; drawing values only where no character says them.

taxon.note: WCVP v16 accepted name Lilium martagon, plant_name_id 279985.

growth_form.note: A bulbous herb with one leafy flowering stem a year, drawn by the forb form.

growth.note: Grown five years from seed, as a lily bulb takes three to five to flower; drawn at its third and fifth years.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

allometry.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): stem 3-6 ft high; Wikipedia 'Lilium martagon': 1-2 m. Its reference height is the middle of that range, 1.35 m, at its last keyframe.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): stem 3-6 ft high; Wikipedia 'Lilium martagon': 1-2 m.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): leaves usually in 2-4 whorls of 6-9 leaves each, with a few scattered ones above; Wikipedia: mostly in whorls.

traits.leaf_whorls.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): usually in 2-4 whorls; var. dalmaticum 5-7.

traits.leaves_per_whorl.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): whorls of 6-9 leaves each. The typical value is our pick of a usual plant inside that range.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): leaves 3-6 in long; Wikipedia: up to 16 cm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): leaves 1-1 1/2 in wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Wikipedia, 'Lilium martagon' (read 2026-10-18): leaves elliptic to inverse lanceolate.

traits.leaf_posture.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): leaves horizontal, deep green.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): flowers 3-20; Wikipedia: up to 50 on vigorous plants. The typical value is our pick of a usual plant inside that range.

traits.flower_posture.note: Flora of China vol. 24, Lilium martagon var. pilosiusculum (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): flowers 2-7 in a raceme, nodding; Bailey's segments reflexed to the stem leave the flower hanging.

traits.perianth_reflexion.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): segments thick, waxy, reflexed to the stem: rolled back until they touch the stalk, drawn as revolute.

traits.flower_colour.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): dull claret-purple; Wikipedia: typically a pink-purple, quite variable. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.perianth_spots.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): spotted purplish black; Wikipedia: with dark spots.

traits.perianth_spot_colour.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): spotted purplish black. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.tepal_length_m.note: Flora of China vol. 24, Lilium martagon var. pilosiusculum (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): tepals 3.2-3.8 cm x 8-9 mm, the only variety it describes; Bailey: flowers 2-3 in diam., which tepals of that length reflexed to the stem give.

traits.anther_colour.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): anthers red. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.bark_colour.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): stem smooth, green, often spotted purple; Wikipedia: green stems can be flushed with purple or red. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of China vol. 24, Lilium martagon var. pilosiusculum (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): capsule obovoid-oblong, 2-2.8 cm.

traits.flowering_months.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): late June, July; Flora of China (var. pilosiusculum): Jun-Jul.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Flora of China vol. 24, Lilium martagon var. pilosiusculum (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): fruit Aug.

traits.shoot_leaves.note: Derived: the stem's leaves are its 2-4 whorls times 6-9 leaves in each, 12-36, from the counts quoted for leaf_whorls (Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): usually in 2-4 whorls; var. dalmaticum 5-7.) and leaves_per_whorl (Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1916), Lilium Martagon, p. 1873 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18): whorls of 6-9 leaves each. The typical value is our pick of a usual plant inside that range.).
